cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Gratitude – the feeling of being thankful and showing appreciation.

p.em: Example: Cultivating deep gratitude in our daily lives has been shown to improve mental well-being.

cosy-blockquote.p: Appreciation – the recognition of the good qualities of someone or something.

p.em: Example: We must show real appreciation for the people who work silently to keep our communities clean.

cosy-blockquote.p: Unsung – not praised, celebrated, or praised publicly despite doing valuable work.

p.em: Example: Cleaners, delivery riders, and social workers are the unsung heroes of our modern cities.

cosy-blockquote.p: Acknowledge – to accept or admit the truth, existence, or value of something.

p.em: Example: It is vital to acknowledge the contributions of every single team member before finishing a project.

cosy-blockquote.p: Kindness – the quality of being friendly, generous, and considerate.

p.em: Example: A small act of kindness can start a positive chain reaction throughout the workplace.

cosy-blockquote.p: Supportive – providing encouragement, help, or emotional assistance to someone.

p.em: Example: Working in a highly supportive environment makes it much easier to handle stressful deadlines.

cosy-blockquote.p: Apathy ≠ Empathy – a lack of enthusiasm, interest, or concern ≠ the ability to understand and share the feelings of another.

p.em: Example: We must actively fight social apathy by teaching empathy and community values in schools.

cosy-blockquote.p: Reciprocate – to respond to a gesture or action by making a corresponding one.

p.em: Example: When someone does you a favor, it is natural to want to reciprocate their kindness in the future.

cosy-blockquote.p: Altruistic – showing a disinterested and selfless concern for the well-being of others.

p.em: Example: His decision to donate all his prize money to the local children's hospital was purely altruistic.

cosy-blockquote.p: Nurture – to care for and encourage the growth or development of someone or something.

p.em: Example: We need to nurture our close relationships by spending quality time together on a regular basis.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
Who is someone whose guidance has fundamentally shaped your career, and what did you do so as to reciprocate?
★ Do you find it natural to articulate your appreciation to professional mentors?

Why does a physical letter, which requires deliberate effort to craft, resonate so much more deeply than an email?
★ When did you last receive a piece of mail that you decided to keep permanently?

How does selecting a highly personalized gift in order to honor a colleague's milestone impact workplace synergy?
★ What is the most thoughtful professional gift you have ever observed?

Is there a specific historical holiday, the origin of which remains controversial, that you utilize to reflect on societal progress?
★ Which national holiday do you think has the most profound historical significance?

What kind of small gesture, which anyone can perform without expense, is most effective to uplift a demoralized peer?
★ How do you usually respond when you notice a colleague is visibly stressed?

Who is a contemporary hero, for whom you have immense respect, and what did they sacrifice so as to defend their principles?
★ Do you think modern media focuses too much on celebrity culture rather than real heroes?

Why is gratitude, which psychologists define as a transformative practice, essential to maintain emotional resilience?
★ What specific aspects of your current life are you most profoundly grateful for?

What community tradition, the survival of which depends entirely on volunteers, is vital to prevent social isolation?
★ How integrated do you feel within your local neighborhood's activities?

Why is proactive kindness, which we often take for granted, a crucial mechanism to bridge cultural divides?
★ Can you recall a time when kindness completely de-escalated a tense situation?

Who is a teacher to whom you are eternally indebted, and what did they do in order to unlock your true potential?
★ How did your favorite educator influence your approach to learning?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative task or visual analysis in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: 💌 Activity 1: The Wall of Gratitude Expressing appreciation strengthens human bonds. Together with your partner, choose a person whom you want to thank today. Draft a short, heartfelt thank-you card to them. Practice using relative clauses (the person whose..., the guide for whom...) and infinitives of purpose (so as to..., in order to...): 👩‍🏫 An Unsung Teacher The mentor whose advice was critical in order to build confidence and resilience. 💼 A Supportive Coworker The colleague whose hard work on a tough project was offered so as to support you. 🏡 A Caring Neighbor The friend upon whom you rely to watch your home in order to prevent worry. 🏆 Closing: The Honorary Tribute If you could establish an official public monument to celebrate one category of unsung heroes, who would you choose to honor today? 🧹 Neighborhood Cleaners & Caretakers 🚴 Spontaneous Delivery Riders & Couriers ❤️ Dedicated Local Charity Volunteers 🚌 Helpful Public Bus & Train Drivers

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
In the future, we will utilize neural monitors that analyze our relationships in order to mandate appreciation intervals.
★ Would you allow an algorithm to dictate when and how you express gratitude?

The tradition of writing a physical letter, which has historically preserved human history, will disappear completely so as to conserve resources.
★ Would the complete death of physical mail represent a major cultural loss for future historians?

A federally mandated appreciation holiday, the parameters of which are strictly enforced, will make emotional expression feel entirely superficial.
★ Is it possible for state-mandated appreciation to ever feel authentic?

Virtual reality will enable us to deliver a sensory gift that simulates real touch in order to bridge the physical gap between distant relatives.
★ Could digital touch ever fully substitute for physical human warmth?

We will develop robotic emergency responders, whose primary directive is to protect human lives in hazardous zones.
★ Would you feel completely secure putting your life in the hands of an autonomous machine?

Future educational systems will incorporate gratitude classes, the success of which will be evaluated using biometric stress-trackers.
★ Do you think measuring emotional sincerity with technology is ethical?

A simple altruistic gesture, which is captured and broadcasted on decentralized feeds, will be leveraged to accumulate social credit.
★ What are the dangers of turning kindness into a tool for public popularity?

The ancient tradition of multi-generational co-habitation, which fosters deep familial bonds, will be abandoned so as to maximize individual mobility.
★ Is the decline of the extended family structure positive or negative for society?

We will establish municipal departments that deploy professional actors in order to perform random acts of kindness in public spaces.
★ Would public kindness lose its magic if you discovered it was a staged municipal performance?

An interactive digital teacher, whose database contains all human knowledge, will replace human educators so as to standardize learning.
★ What essential human qualities does an AI teacher lack that are vital for mentoring youth?

ul.li: Incorrect: I am very grateful of my teacher. → Correct: I am very grateful to my teacher / grateful for my teacher's help. ((Preposition check: 'grateful' is followed by 'to' for people, and 'for' for actions/things.))
Incorrect: We discussed about our someone special. → Correct: We discussed our special someone. ((Preposition error: the verb 'discuss' is transitive and does not take 'about'.))
Incorrect: It is very important to nurturing friendships. → Correct: It is very important to nurture friendships. ((Infinitive structure: 'to' is followed by the base form of the verb 'nurture'.))
